pick.name: Better Auth
pick.what: TypeScript auth framework: email/password, OAuth, 2FA, passkeys, orgs/multi-tenant, SSO plugin
pick.why: MIT, no per-MAU fees, users live in your own Postgres (good for regulated buyers), and Auth.js is now maintained under it
pick.free_limits: Library; unlimited users; you host it

alts.name: WorkOS AuthKit
alts.why: Pay-later pick for enterprise: 1M MAU free, then sells SSO per connection
alts.free_limits: AuthKit first 1M MAU free; SSO / Directory Sync $125 per connection (1-15); custom domain $99/mo

alts.name: Clerk Hobby
alts.why: Fastest hosted DX, but free plan lacks MFA/passkeys/SSO
alts.free_limits: 50k MRU/app; 'Secured by Clerk' branding; no MFA, passkeys, SMS, SSO on free; Pro $25/mo ($20 annual)

candidates.name: Better Auth
candidates.verdict: PICK: MIT, self-owned data, plugins for orgs/2FA/passkeys/SSO; Auth.js joined it Sept 2025

candidates.name: WorkOS AuthKit
candidates.verdict: Alt: when an enterprise buyer demands SAML/SCIM quickly (pay per connection)

candidates.name: Clerk
candidates.verdict: Alt: fastest UI, but vendor-held users and limited free security features

candidates.name: Supabase Auth
candidates.verdict: Good if all-in on Supabase (50k MAU free)

candidates.name: Neon Auth
candidates.verdict: Bundled with Neon (60k MAU/project free on pricing page); newer

candidates.name: Auth.js
candidates.verdict: Now maintained by Better Auth team; Better Auth recommends new projects use Better Auth

candidates.name: Logto / Keycloak / SuperTokens
candidates.verdict: Self-hosted IdP servers: more ops; Keycloak heavy; SuperTokens Apache-2.0

decision: Better Auth gives you auth you own with no MAU bill and Claude Code-friendly typed APIs; it also absorbed Auth.js. Add WorkOS only when an enterprise contract requires SAML/SCIM and you don't want to run SSO yourself.
details: Password hashing on Workers Free may exceed 10 ms CPU; use OAuth/magic link/passkeys or Workers Paid. Exact SSO/SAML plugin maturity not verified.

verify.note: Shallow check only (npm version as recorded). MIT library, no MAU fees.
